Throughout the entire day on Tuesday, the Twitter feed of Benjamin Netanyahu,
the leader of the "only democracy in the Middle East," was filled with
desperate pleas, warning Israeli Jews that Arabs were turning out in record
numbers.

It wasn't just Arabs or, more accurately, Palestinian citizens of Israel.
Turnout in the Israeli election was 77.7%, the highest since 1999. The voters
delivered a sharp rebuke to Netanyahu, but what happens next is up in the air.

As of 12:20 local time (10:20 GMT), the Netanyahu-led bloc of parties had lost
about 14 seats, with the collective holding onto 54 seats, per partial results
from Israel's Central Elections Committee. The opposition bloc led by [Gadi
Eisenkot](https://zeteo.com/p/meet-the-5-israeli-politicians-trying) netted 47
seats. Arab-led parties secured 19 seats, almost doubling the 10 they
previously held.

To secure a majority, 61 seats or more are needed.
